id.description: The ID of the work item to retrieve.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

fields.description: Optional list of fields to include in the response. If not provided, all fields will be returned.

asOf.description: Optional date string to retrieve the work item as of a specific time. If not provided, the current state will be returned.

expand.description: Expand options include 'all', 'fields', 'links', 'none', and 'relations'. Relations can be used to get child workitems. Defaults to 'none'.

tools.name: wit_list_work_item_comments
tools.description: Retrieve list of comments for a work item by ID.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item to retrieve comments for.

top.description: Optional number of comments to retrieve. Defaults to all comments.

tools.name: wit_add_work_item_comment
tools.description: Add comment to a work item by ID.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item to add a comment to.

comment.description: The text of the comment to add to the work item.

tools.name: wit_add_child_work_items
tools.description: Create one or many child work items from a parent by work item type and parent id.

parentId.description: The ID of the parent work item to create a child work item under.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

workItemType.description: The type of the child work item to create.

title.description: The title of the child work item.

description.description: The description of the child work item.

format.description: Format for the description on the child work item, e.g., 'Markdown', 'Html'. Defaults to 'Html'.

areaPath.description: Optional area path for the child work item.

iterationPath.description: Optional iteration path for the child work item.

tools.name: wit_link_work_item_to_pull_request
tools.description: Link a single work item to an existing pull request.

projectId.description: The project ID of the Azure DevOps project (note: project name is not valid).

repositoryId.description: The ID of the repository containing the pull request. Do not use the repository name here, use the ID instead.

pullRequestId.description: The ID of the pull request to link to.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item to link to the pull request.

pullRequestProjectId.description: The project ID containing the pull request. If not provided, defaults to the work item's project ID (for same-project linking).

tools.name: wit_get_work_items_for_iteration
tools.description: Retrieve a list of work items for a specified iteration.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. If not provided, the default team will be used.

iterationId.description: The ID of the iteration to retrieve work items for.

tools.name: wit_update_work_item
tools.description: Update a work item by ID with specified fields.

id.description: The ID of the work item to update.

op.description: The operation to perform on the field.

path.description: The path of the field to update, e.g., '/fields/System.Title'.

value.description: The new value for the field. This is required for 'Add' and 'Replace' operations, and should be omitted for 'Remove' operations.

updates.description: An array of field updates to apply to the work item.

tools.name: wit_get_work_item_type
tools.description: Get a specific work item type.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

workItemType.description: The name of the work item type to retrieve.

tools.name: wit_create_work_item
tools.description: Create a new work item in a specified project and work item type.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

workItemType.description: The type of work item to create, e.g., 'Task', 'Bug', etc.

name.description: The name of the field, e.g., 'System.Title'.

value.description: The value of the field.

format.description: the format of the field value, e.g., 'Html', 'Markdown'. Optional, defaults to 'Html'.

fields.description: A record of field names and values to set on the new work item. Each fild is the field name and each value is the corresponding value to set for that field.

tools.name: wit_get_query
tools.description: Get a query by its ID or path.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

query.description: The ID or path of the query to retrieve.

expand.description: Optional expand parameter to include additional details in the response. Defaults to 'None'.

depth.description: Optional depth parameter to specify how deep to expand the query. Defaults to 0.

includeDeleted.description: Whether to include deleted items in the query results. Defaults to false.

useIsoDateFormat.description: Whether to use ISO date format in the response. Defaults to false.

tools.name: wit_get_query_results_by_id
tools.description: Retrieve the results of a work item query given the query ID.

id.description: The ID of the query to retrieve results for.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. If not provided, the default project will be used.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. If not provided, the default team will be used.

timePrecision.description: Whether to include time precision in the results. Defaults to false.

top.description: The maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: wit_update_work_items_batch
tools.description: Update work items in batch

op.description: The operation to perform on the field.

id.description: The ID of the work item to update.

path.description: The path of the field to update, e.g., '/fields/System.Title'.

value.description: The new value for the field. This is required for 'add' and 'replace' operations, and should be omitted for 'remove' operations.

format.description: The format of the field value. Only to be used for large text fields. e.g., 'Html', 'Markdown'. Optional, defaults to 'Html'.

updates.description: An array of updates to apply to work items. Each update should include the operation (op), work item ID (id), field path (path), and new value (value).

tools.name: wit_work_items_link
tools.description: Link work items together in batch.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

id.description: The ID of the work item to update.

linkToId.description: The ID of the work item to link to.

type.description: Type of link to create between the work items. Options include 'parent', 'child', 'duplicate', 'duplicate of', 'related', 'successor', 'predecessor', 'tested by', 'tests', 'affects', and 'affected by'. Defaults to 'related'.

comment.description: Optional comment to include with the link. This can be used to provide additional context for the link being created.

tools.name: wit_work_item_unlink
tools.description: Remove one or many links from a single work item

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

id.description: The ID of the work item to remove the links from.

type.description: Type of link to remove. Options include 'parent', 'child', 'duplicate', 'duplicate of', 'related', 'successor', 'predecessor', 'tested by', 'tests', 'affects', 'affected by', and 'artifact'. Defaults to 'related'.

url.description: Optional URL to match for the link to remove. If not provided, all links of the specified type will be removed.

tools.name: wit_add_artifact_link
tools.description: Add artifact links (repository, branch, commit, builds) to work items. You can either provide the full vstfs URI or the individual components to build it automatically.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item to add the artifact link to.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

artifactUri.description: The complete VSTFS URI of the artifact to link. If provided, individual component parameters are ignored.

projectId.description: The project ID (GUID) containing the artifact. Required for Git artifacts when artifactUri is not provided.

repositoryId.description: The repository ID (GUID) containing the artifact. Required for Git artifacts when artifactUri is not provided.

branchName.description: The branch name (e.g., 'main'). Required when linkType is 'Branch'.

commitId.description: The commit SHA hash. Required when linkType is 'Fixed in Commit'.

pullRequestId.description: The pull request ID. Required when linkType is 'Pull Request'.

buildId.description: The build ID. Required when linkType is 'Build', 'Found in build', or 'Integrated in build'.

linkType.description: Type of artifact link, defaults to 'Branch'. This determines both the link type and how to build the VSTFS URI from individual components.

comment.description: Comment to include with the artifact link.

project.description: The project name or ID where the wiki is located. If not provided, the default project will be used.

tools.name: wiki_list_pages
tools.description: Retrieve a list of wiki pages for a specific wiki and project.

wikiIdentifier.description: The unique identifier of the wiki.

project.description: The project name or ID where the wiki is located.

top.description: The maximum number of pages to return. Defaults to 20.

continuationToken.description: Token for pagination to retrieve the next set of pages.

pageViewsForDays.description: Number of days to retrieve page views for. If not specified, page views are not included.

tools.name: wiki_get_page
tools.description: Retrieve wiki page metadata by path. This tool does not return page content.

wikiIdentifier.description: The unique identifier of the wiki.

project.description: The project name or ID where the wiki is located.

path.description: The path of the wiki page (e.g., '/Home' or '/Documentation/Setup').

recursionLevel.description: Recursion level for subpages. 'None' returns only the specified page. 'OneLevel' includes direct children. 'Full' includes all descendants.

tools.name: wiki_get_page_content
tools.description: Retrieve wiki page content. Provide either a 'url' parameter OR the combination of 'wikiIdentifier' and 'project' parameters.

url.description: The full URL of the wiki page to retrieve content for. If provided, wikiIdentifier, project, and path are ignored. Supported patterns: https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_wiki/wikis/{wikiIdentifier}?pagePath=%2FMy%20Page and https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_wiki/wikis/{wikiIdentifier}/{pageId}/Page-Title

wikiIdentifier.description: The unique identifier of the wiki. Required if url is not provided.

project.description: The project name or ID where the wiki is located. Required if url is not provided.

path.description: The path of the wiki page to retrieve content for. Optional, defaults to root page if not provided.

tools.name: wiki_create_or_update_page
tools.description: Create or update a wiki page with content.

wikiIdentifier.description: The unique identifier or name of the wiki.

path.description: The path of the wiki page (e.g., '/Home' or '/Documentation/Setup').

content.description: The content of the wiki page in markdown format.

project.description: The project name or ID where the wiki is located. If not provided, the default project will be used.

etag.description: ETag for editing existing pages (optional, will be fetched if not provided).

branch.description: The branch name for the wiki repository. Defaults to 'wikiMaster' which is the default branch for Azure DevOps wikis.

repositoryId.description: The ID of the repository where the pull request is located.

pullRequestId.description: The ID of the pull request to retrieve changes for.

iterationId.description: The iteration ID to get changes for. If not specified, gets changes for the latest iteration.

project.description: Project ID or project name (optional)

top.description: Maximum number of files to include diffs for. Default is 100.

skip.description: Number of changes to skip for pagination.

compareTo.description: Iteration ID to compare against. If specified, returns changes between two iterations.

includeDiffs.description: Whether to include actual line-by-line diff content. Default is true. Set to false to get only file metadata.

includeLineContent.description: Whether to include the actual line content from the changed files. Default is true. When true, fetches file content and includes the actual code lines that were added/removed/modified.

tools.name: repo_reply_to_comment
tools.description: Replies to a specific comment on a pull request.

repositoryId.description: The ID or name of the repository where the pull request is located. When using a repository name instead of a GUID, the project parameter must also be provided.

pullRequestId.description: The ID of the pull request where the comment thread exists.

threadId.description: The ID of the thread to which the comment will be added.

content.description: The content of the comment to be added.

project.description: Project ID or project name. Required when repositoryId is a repository name instead of a GUID.

fullResponse.description: Return full comment JSON response instead of a simple confirmation message.

tools.name: repo_create_pull_request_thread
tools.description: Creates a new comment thread on a pull request.

repositoryId.description: The ID or name of the repository where the pull request is located. When using a repository name instead of a GUID, the project parameter must also be provided.

pullRequestId.description: The ID of the pull request where the comment thread exists.

content.description: The content of the comment to be added.

project.description: Project ID or project name. Required when repositoryId is a repository name instead of a GUID.

filePath.description: The path of the file where the comment thread will be created. (optional)

status.description: The status of the comment thread. Defaults to 'Active'.

rightFileStartLine.description: Position of first character of the thread's span in right file. The line number of a thread's position. Starts at 1. (optional)

rightFileStartOffset.description: Position of first character of the thread's span in right file. The line number of a thread's position. The character offset of a thread's position inside of a line. Starts at 1. Must be set if rightFileStartLine is also specified. (optional)

rightFileEndLine.description: Position of last character of the thread's span in right file. The line number of a thread's position. Starts at 1. Must be set if rightFileStartLine is also specified. (optional)

rightFileEndOffset.description: Position of last character of the thread's span in right file. The character offset of a thread's position inside of a line. Must be set if rightFileEndLine is also specified. (optional)

tools.name: repo_update_pull_request_thread
tools.description: Updates an existing comment thread on a pull request.

repositoryId.description: The ID or name of the repository where the pull request is located. When using a repository name instead of a GUID, the project parameter must also be provided.

pullRequestId.description: The ID of the pull request where the comment thread exists.

threadId.description: The ID of the thread to update.

project.description: Project ID or project name. Required when repositoryId is a repository name instead of a GUID.

status.description: The new status for the comment thread.

tools.name: repo_search_commits
tools.description: Search for commits in a repository with comprehensive filtering capabilities. Supports searching by description/comment text, time range, author, committer, specific commit IDs, and more. This is the unified tool for all commit search operations.

project.description: Project name or ID

version.description: The name of the branch, tag or commit to filter commits by

versionType.description: The meaning of the version parameter, e.g., branch, tag or commit

skip.description: Number of commits to skip

top.description: Maximum number of commits to return

searchText.description: Search text to filter commits by description/comment. Supports partial matching.

author.description: Filter commits by author email or display name

authorEmail.description: Filter commits by exact author email address

committer.description: Filter commits by committer email or display name

committerEmail.description: Filter commits by exact committer email address

fromDate.description: Filter commits from this date (ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')

toDate.description: Filter commits to this date (ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z')

commitIds.description: Array of specific commit IDs to retrieve. When provided, other filters are ignored except top/skip.

historySimplificationMode.description: How to simplify the commit history

tools.name: repo_list_pull_requests_by_commits
tools.description: Lists pull requests by commit IDs to find which pull requests contain specific commits

project.description: Project name or ID

commits.description: Array of commit IDs to query for

tools.name: repo_vote_pull_request
tools.description: Cast a vote on a pull request. Automatically adds the current user as a reviewer if they are not already one.

repositoryId.description: The ID or name of the repository. When using a repository name instead of a GUID, the project parameter must also be provided.

pullRequestId.description: The ID of the pull request.

vote.description: The vote to cast: Approved(10), Suggestions(5), None(0), Waiting(-5), Rejected(-10).

project.description: Project ID or project name. Required when repositoryId is a repository name instead of a GUID.

tools.name: repo_list_directory
tools.description: List files and folders in a directory within a repository. Useful for exploring the structure of a codebase or finding related files.

repositoryId.description: The ID or name of the repository.

path.description: The directory path to list (e.g., '/src' or '/src/components'). Defaults to repository root.

project.description: Project ID or name. Required if repositoryId is a name rather than a GUID.

version.description: The version identifier - branch name (e.g., 'main'), tag name, or commit SHA. Defaults to the repository's default branch.

versionType.description: The type of version identifier: 'Branch', 'Commit', or 'Tag'. Defaults to 'Branch'.

recursive.description: Whether to list items recursively. Defaults to false.

recursionDepth.description: Maximum depth for recursive listing (1-10). Only applies when recursive is true. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: repo_get_file_content
tools.description: Get the content of a file from a Git repository at a specific version (branch, tag, or commit SHA). Useful for reading source files from PR branches, specific commits, or tags without having them checked out locally.

repositoryId.description: The ID (GUID) or name of the repository.

path.description: The full path to the file in the repository, e.g., '/src/main.ts' or 'src/main.ts'.

project.description: Project ID or project name. Required when repositoryId is a name.

version.description: Version string: branch name (e.g. 'main'), tag name, or commit SHA. Defaults to the repository's default branch if not specified.

versionType.description: How to interpret the 'version' parameter. Defaults to 'Commit'.

tools.name: wit_list_backlogs
tools.description: Receive a list of backlogs for a given project and team. If a project or team is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a team selection prompt will be shown.

tools.name: wit_list_backlog_work_items
tools.description: Retrieve a list of backlogs of for a given project, team, and backlog category. If a project or team is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a team selection prompt will be shown.

backlogId.description: The ID of the backlog category to retrieve work items from.

tools.name: wit_my_work_items
tools.description: Retrieve a list of work items relevent to the authenticated user. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

type.description: The type of work items to retrieve. Defaults to 'assignedtome'.

top.description: The maximum number of work items to return. Defaults to 50.

includeCompleted.description: Whether to include completed work items. Defaults to false.

tools.name: wit_get_work_items_batch_by_ids
tools.description: Retrieve list of work items by IDs in batch. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

ids.description: The IDs of the work items to retrieve.

fields.description: Optional list of fields to include in the response. If not provided, a hardcoded default set of fields will be used.

tools.name: wit_get_work_item
tools.description: Get a single work item by ID. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

id.description: The ID of the work item to retrieve.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

fields.description: Optional list of fields to include in the response. If not provided, all fields will be returned. Cannot be used together with the expand parameter.

asOf.description: Optional date string to retrieve the work item as of a specific time. If not provided, the current state will be returned.

expand.description: Expand options include 'All', 'Fields', 'Links', 'None', and 'Relations'. Relations can be used to get child workitems. Defaults to 'None'. Cannot be used together with the fields parameter.

tools.name: wit_list_work_item_comments
tools.description: Retrieve list of comments for a work item by ID. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item to retrieve comments for.

top.description: Optional number of comments to retrieve. Defaults to all comments.

tools.name: wit_add_work_item_comment
tools.description: Add comment to a work item by ID. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item to add a comment to.

comment.description: The text of the comment to add to the work item.

format.description: The format of the comment text, e.g., 'Markdown', 'Html'. Optional, defaults to 'Markdown'.

tools.name: wit_update_work_item_comment
tools.description: Update an existing comment on a work item by ID. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item.

commentId.description: The ID of the comment to update.

text.description: The updated comment text.

format.description: The format of the comment text, e.g., 'Markdown', 'Html'. Optional, defaults to 'Markdown'.

tools.name: wit_list_work_item_revisions
tools.description: Retrieve list of revisions for a work item by ID. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item to retrieve revisions for.

top.description: Optional number of revisions to retrieve. If not provided, all revisions will be returned.

skip.description: Optional number of revisions to skip for pagination. Defaults to 0.

expand.description: Optional expand parameter to include additional details. Defaults to 'None'.

tools.name: wit_add_child_work_items
tools.description: Create one or many child work items from a parent by work item type and parent id. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

parentId.description: The ID of the parent work item to create a child work item under.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

workItemType.description: The type of the child work item to create.

title.description: The title of the child work item.

description.description: The description of the child work item.

format.description: Format for the description on the child work item, e.g., 'Markdown', 'Html'. Defaults to 'Markdown'.

areaPath.description: Optional area path for the child work item.

iterationPath.description: Optional iteration path for the child work item.

tools.name: wit_link_work_item_to_pull_request
tools.description: Link a single work item to an existing pull request.

projectId.description: The project ID of the Azure DevOps project (note: project name is not valid).

repositoryId.description: The ID of the repository containing the pull request. Do not use the repository name here, use the ID instead.

pullRequestId.description: The ID of the pull request to link to.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item to link to the pull request.

pullRequestProjectId.description: The project ID containing the pull request. If not provided, defaults to the work item's project ID (for same-project linking).

tools.name: wit_get_work_items_for_iteration
tools.description: Retrieve a list of work items for a specified iteration. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. If not provided, the default team will be used.

iterationId.description: The ID of the iteration to retrieve work items for.

tools.name: wit_update_work_item
tools.description: Update a work item by ID with specified fields.

id.description: The ID of the work item to update.

op.description: The operation to perform on the field.

path.description: The path of the field to update, e.g., '/fields/System.Title'.

value.description: The new value for the field. This is required for 'Add' and 'Replace' operations, and should be omitted for 'Remove' operations.

updates.description: An array of field updates to apply to the work item.

tools.name: wit_get_work_item_type
tools.description: Get a specific work item type. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

workItemType.description: The name of the work item type to retrieve.

tools.name: wit_create_work_item
tools.description: Create a new work item in a specified project and work item type. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

workItemType.description: The type of work item to create, e.g., 'Task', 'Bug', etc.

name.description: The name of the field, e.g., 'System.Title'.

value.description: The value of the field.

format.description: the format of the field value, e.g., 'Html', 'Markdown'. Optional, defaults to 'Markdown'.

fields.description: A record of field names and values to set on the new work item. Each fild is the field name and each value is the corresponding value to set for that field.

tools.name: wit_get_query
tools.description: Get a query by its ID or path. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

query.description: The ID or path of the query to retrieve.

expand.description: Optional expand parameter to include additional details in the response. Defaults to 'None'.

depth.description: Optional depth parameter to specify how deep to expand the query. Defaults to 0.

includeDeleted.description: Whether to include deleted items in the query results. Defaults to false.

useIsoDateFormat.description: Whether to use ISO date format in the response. Defaults to false.

tools.name: wit_get_query_results_by_id
tools.description: Retrieve the results of a work item query given the query ID. Supports full or IDs-only response types.

id.description: The ID of the query to retrieve results for.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. If not provided, the default project will be used.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. If not provided, the default team will be used.

timePrecision.description: Whether to include time precision in the results. Defaults to false.

top.description: The maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 50.

responseType.description: Response type: 'full' returns complete query results (default), 'ids' returns only work item IDs for reduced payload size.

tools.name: wit_update_work_items_batch
tools.description: Update work items in batch

op.description: The operation to perform on the field.

id.description: The ID of the work item to update.

path.description: The path of the field to update, e.g., '/fields/System.Title'.

value.description: The new value for the field. This is required for 'add' and 'replace' operations, and should be omitted for 'remove' operations.

format.description: The format of the field value. Only to be used for large text fields. e.g., 'Html', 'Markdown'. Optional, defaults to 'Markdown'.

updates.description: An array of updates to apply to work items. Each update should include the operation (op), work item ID (id), field path (path), and new value (value).

tools.name: wit_work_items_link
tools.description: Link work items together in batch. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

id.description: The ID of the work item to update.

linkToId.description: The ID of the work item to link to.

type.description: Type of link to create between the work items. Options include 'parent', 'child', 'duplicate', 'duplicate of', 'related', 'successor', 'predecessor', 'tested by', 'tests', 'affects', and 'affected by'. Defaults to 'related'.

comment.description: Optional comment to include with the link. This can be used to provide additional context for the link being created.

tools.name: wit_work_item_unlink
tools.description: Remove one or many links from a single work item. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

id.description: The ID of the work item to remove the links from.

type.description: Type of link to remove. Options include 'parent', 'child', 'duplicate', 'duplicate of', 'related', 'successor', 'predecessor', 'tested by', 'tests', 'affects', 'affected by', and 'artifact'. Defaults to 'related'.

url.description: Optional URL to match for the link to remove. If not provided, all links of the specified type will be removed.

tools.name: wit_add_artifact_link
tools.description: Add artifact links (repository, branch, commit, builds) to work items. You can either provide the full vstfs URI or the individual components to build it automatically. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item to add the artifact link to.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

artifactUri.description: The complete VSTFS URI of the artifact to link. If provided, individual component parameters are ignored.

projectId.description: The project ID (GUID) containing the artifact. Required for Git artifacts when artifactUri is not provided.

repositoryId.description: The repository ID (GUID) containing the artifact. Required for Git artifacts when artifactUri is not provided.

branchName.description: The branch name (e.g., 'main'). Required when linkType is 'Branch'.

commitId.description: The commit SHA hash. Required when linkType is 'Fixed in Commit'.

pullRequestId.description: The pull request ID. Required when linkType is 'Pull Request'.

buildId.description: The build ID. Required when linkType is 'Build', 'Found in build', or 'Integrated in build'.

linkType.description: Type of artifact link, defaults to 'Branch'. This determines both the link type and how to build the VSTFS URI from individual components.

comment.description: Comment to include with the artifact link.

tools.name: wit_query_by_wiql
tools.description: Execute a WIQL (Work Item Query Language) query and return the matching work items. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

wiql.description: The WIQL query string to execute, e.g., "SELECT [System.Id], [System.Title] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.TeamProject] = @project"

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. If not provided, the default team context will be used.

timePrecision.description: Whether to include time precision in date fields. Defaults to false.

top.description: The maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: wit_get_work_item_attachment
tools.description: Download a work item attachment by its ID and return the content as a base64-encoded resource. Useful for viewing images (e.g. screenshots) attached to work items such as bugs. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

attachmentId.description: The GUID of the attachment. Found in the attachment URL: https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_apis/wit/attachments/{attachmentId}

fileName.description: The file name of the attachment, e.g. 'screenshot.png'. Used to determine the MIME type for the returned resource.

wikiIdentifier.description: The unique identifier of the wiki.

project.description: The project name or ID where the wiki is located. If not provided, the default project will be used.

tools.name: wiki_list_pages

wikiIdentifier.description: The unique identifier of the wiki.

pageViewsForDays.description: Number of days to retrieve page views for. If not specified, page views are not included.

wikiIdentifier.description: The unique identifier of the wiki.

project.description: The project name or ID where the wiki is located.

tools.name: wiki_get_page_content
tools.description: Retrieve wiki page content. Provide either a 'url' parameter OR the combination of 'wikiIdentifier' and 'project' parameters.

url.description: The full URL of the wiki page to retrieve content for. If provided, wikiIdentifier, project, and path are ignored. Supported patterns: https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_wiki/wikis/{wikiIdentifier}?pagePath=%2FMy%20Page and https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_wiki/wikis/{wikiIdentifier}/{pageId}/Page-Title

wikiIdentifier.description: The unique identifier of the wiki. Required if url is not provided.

project.description: The project name or ID where the wiki is located. Required if url is not provided.

path.description: The path of the wiki page to retrieve content for. Optional, defaults to root page if not provided.

tools.name: wiki_create_or_update_page
tools.description: Create or update a wiki page with content.

wikiIdentifier.description: The unique identifier or name of the wiki.

path.description: The path of the wiki page (e.g., '/Home' or '/Documentation/Setup').

content.description: The content of the wiki page in markdown format.

project.description: The project name or ID where the wiki is located. If not provided, the default project will be used.

etag.description: ETag for editing existing pages (optional, will be fetched if not provided).

branch.description: The branch name for the wiki repository. Defaults to 'wikiMaster' which is the default branch for Azure DevOps wikis.

workItemType.description: The name of the work item type to retrieve.

workItemType.description: The type of work item to create, e.g., 'Task', 'Bug', etc.

name.description: The name of the field, e.g., 'System.Title'.

value.description: The value of the field.

format.description: the format of the field value, e.g., 'Html', 'Markdown'. Optional, defaults to 'Markdown'.

tools.name: wit_get_query

useIsoDateFormat.description: Whether to use ISO date format in the response. Defaults to false.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. If not provided, the default project will be used.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. If not provided, the default team will be used.

timePrecision.description: Whether to include time precision in the results. Defaults to false.

tools.name: wit_update_work_items_batch
tools.description: Update work items in batch

op.description: The operation to perform on the field.

id.description: The ID of the work item to update.

path.description: The path of the field to update, e.g., '/fields/System.Title'.

value.description: The new value for the field. This is required for 'add' and 'replace' operations, and should be omitted for 'remove' operations.

format.description: The format of the field value. Only to be used for large text fields. e.g., 'Html', 'Markdown'. Optional, defaults to 'Markdown'.

updates.description: An array of updates to apply to work items. Each update should include the operation (op), work item ID (id), field path (path), and new value (value).

tools.name: wit_work_items_link
tools.description: Link work items together in batch. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

id.description: The ID of the work item to update.

linkToId.description: The ID of the work item to link to.

type.description: Type of link to create between the work items. Options include 'parent', 'child', 'duplicate', 'duplicate of', 'related', 'successor', 'predecessor', 'tested by', 'tests', 'affects', and 'affected by'. Defaults to 'related'.

comment.description: Optional comment to include with the link. This can be used to provide additional context for the link being created.

tools.name: wit_work_item_unlink
tools.description: Remove one or many links from a single work item. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

id.description: The ID of the work item to remove the links from.

type.description: Type of link to remove. Options include 'parent', 'child', 'duplicate', 'duplicate of', 'related', 'successor', 'predecessor', 'tested by', 'tests', 'affects', 'affected by', and 'artifact'. Defaults to 'related'.

url.description: Optional URL to match for the link to remove. If not provided, all links of the specified type will be removed.

tools.name: wit_add_artifact_link
tools.description: Add artifact links (repository, branch, commit, builds) to work items. You can either provide the full vstfs URI or the individual components to build it automatically. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item to add the artifact link to.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

artifactUri.description: The complete VSTFS URI of the artifact to link. If provided, individual component parameters are ignored.

projectId.description: The project ID (GUID) containing the artifact. Required for Git artifacts when artifactUri is not provided.

repositoryId.description: The repository ID (GUID) containing the artifact. Required for Git artifacts when artifactUri is not provided.

branchName.description: The branch name (e.g., 'main'). Required when linkType is 'Branch'.

commitId.description: The commit SHA hash. Required when linkType is 'Fixed in Commit'.

pullRequestId.description: The pull request ID. Required when linkType is 'Pull Request'.

buildId.description: The build ID. Required when linkType is 'Build', 'Found in build', or 'Integrated in build'.

wikiId.description: The wiki ID (GUID). Required when linkType is 'Wiki'.

pageId.description: The numeric wiki page ID from the browser URL (e.g., '98' in '.../wikis/Contoso.wiki/98/What-is-Contoso'). When provided for 'Wiki' links, the full page path is resolved automatically via the API. Takes precedence over 'pagePath'.

pagePath.description: The full wiki page path from the wiki root (e.g., '/Home/What-is-Contoso'). Required when linkType is 'Wiki' and 'pageId' is not provided. Must be the complete path, not just the page name from the URL.

linkType.description: Type of artifact link, defaults to 'Branch'. This determines both the link type and how to build the VSTFS URI from individual components.

comment.description: Comment to include with the artifact link.

tools.name: wit_query_by_wiql
tools.description: Execute a WIQL (Work Item Query Language) query and return the matching work items. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

wiql.description: The WIQL query string to execute, e.g., "SELECT [System.Id], [System.Title] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.TeamProject] = @project"

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. If not provided, the default team context will be used.

timePrecision.description: Whether to include time precision in date fields. Defaults to false.

top.description: The maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: wit_get_work_item_attachment
tools.description: Download a work item attachment by its ID. By default returns the content as a base64-encoded resource. If savePath is provided, saves the file locally to that directory and returns the file path instead. Useful for viewing images (e.g. screenshots) or other files attached to work items such as bugs. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

attachmentId.description: The GUID of the attachment. Found in the attachment URL: https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_apis/wit/attachments/{attachmentId}

fileName.description: The file name of the attachment, e.g. 'screenshot.png'. Used to determine the MIME type or the saved file's name.

savePath.description: Optional local directory path where the file should be saved. Must be a relative path (e.g. 'temp' or 'downloads/attachments'); absolute paths and path traversals are not allowed. If provided, saves the attachment to this directory and returns the file path. If omitted, returns the content as a base64-encoded resource.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. Required for list_team_iterations, get_team_settings, and get_team_capacity. Reuse from prior context if already known.

team.description: The name or Id of the Azure DevOps team.

teamMemberId.description: The team member Id for the specific team member.

iterationId.description: The Iteration Id to update the capacity for.

name.description: The name of the activity (e.g., 'Development').

capacityPerDay.description: The capacity per day for this activity.

activities.description: Array of activities and their daily capacities for the team member.

start.description: Start date of the day off in ISO format.

end.description: End date of the day off in ISO format.

daysOff.description: Array of days off for the team member, each with a start and end date in ISO format.

reasonFilter.description: Reason filter (see BuildReason enum). Used for: list.

statusFilter.description: Status filter (see BuildStatus enum). Used for: list.

resultFilter.description: Result filter (see BuildResult enum). Used for: list.

tagFilters.description: Array of tags to filter builds. Used for: list.

top.description: Maximum number of builds to return. Used for: list, get_changes.

continuationToken.description: Token for continuing paged results. Used for: list, get_changes.

maxBuildsPerDefinition.description: Maximum number of builds per definition. Used for: list.

deletedFilter.description: Filter for deleted builds (see QueryDeletedOption enum). Used for: list.

queryOrder.description: Order in which builds are returned (BuildQueryOrder values). Used for: list.

branchName.description: Branch name to filter builds. Used for: list.

buildIds.description: Array of specific build IDs to retrieve. Used for: list.

repositoryId.description: Repository ID to filter builds. Used for: list.

repositoryType.description: Repository type to filter builds. Used for: list.

includeSourceChange.description: Whether to include source changes in results. Used for: get_changes.

project.description: The unique identifier (ID or name) of the Azure DevOps project. Required for: create.

title.description: The title of the test case. Required for: create.

priority.description: The priority of the test case. Used for: create.

areaPath.description: The area path for the test case. Used for: create.

iterationPath.description: The iteration path for the test case. Used for: create.

testsWorkItemId.description: Work item ID to set as a Microsoft.VSTS.Common.TestedBy-Reverse link. Used for: create.

id.description: The ID of the test case work item to update. Required for: update_steps.

steps.description:
The steps for the test case. Format each step as '1. Step one|Expected result one
2. Step two|Expected result two'. Use '|' as the delimiter between step and expected result. Required for: update_steps. Used for: create.

tools.name: advsec_get_alerts
tools.description: Retrieve Advanced Security alerts for a repository. Results are scoped to the specified project and repository. Branch filters (onlyDefaultBranch, ref) apply only to code, dependency, and license alerts; they are not applicable to secret alerts and are ignored by the service, so they neither include nor exclude secrets. To narrow secret alerts by confidence, pass a single 'confidenceLevels' value ('High' or 'Other'); selecting every level is treated as no confidence filter.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

repository.description: The name or ID of the repository to get alerts for.

alertType.description: Filter alerts by type. If not specified, returns all alert types.

states.description: Filter alerts by state. If not specified, returns alerts in any state.

severities.description: Filter alerts by severity level. If not specified, returns alerts at any severity.

ref.description: Filter non-secret alerts by git reference (branch), e.g. 'refs/heads/main'. When omitted and onlyDefaultBranch is true, only alerts on the default branch are returned. Not applicable to secret alerts and ignored by this tool when alertType is 'Secret'. When alertType is unspecified, this filter is still sent and may exclude secret alerts from the results; query alertType 'Secret' separately to retrieve all secrets.

onlyDefaultBranch.description: For non-secret alerts: if true (the service default when omitted) only return alerts found on the default branch; if false, return alerts from all branches. Ignored when 'ref' is provided. Not applicable to secret alerts and ignored by this tool when alertType is 'Secret'. When alertType is unspecified, this filter is still sent and may exclude secret alerts from the results; query alertType 'Secret' separately to retrieve all secrets.

confidenceLevels.description: Only applicable to secret alerts. Accepted values are 'High' and 'Other'. Pass a single value (e.g. ['High']) to narrow secrets to that confidence level. Leave unset to return secrets without a confidence filter. Do not select both levels to widen results: the Alerts service does not accept a multi-value confidence filter and would return no alerts, so this tool treats an all-levels selection as no filter and omits it.

validity.description: Only applicable to secret alerts. If omitted, alerts of all validity statuses are returned (no validity filter is applied). Filtering by validity may return fewer alerts than 'top'; use the continuation token to fetch any remaining alerts.

top.description: Maximum number of alerts to return. Defaults to 100.

orderBy.description: Order results by specified field. Defaults to 'severity'.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

tools.name: logo_search
tools.description:
Search and return logos in specified format (JSX, TSX, SVG).
Supports single and multiple logo searches with category filtering.
Can return logos in different themes (light/dark) if available.

When to use this tool:
1. When user types "/logo" command (e.g., "/logo GitHub")
2. When user asks to add a company logo that's not in the local project

Example queries:
- Single company: ["discord"]
- Multiple companies: ["discord", "github", "slack"]
- Specific brand: ["microsoft office"]
- Command style: "/logo GitHub" -> ["github"]
- Request style: "Add Discord logo to the project" -> ["discord"]

Format options:
- TSX: Returns TypeScript React component
- JSX: Returns JavaScript React component
- SVG: Returns raw SVG markup

Each result includes:
- Component name (e.g., DiscordIcon)
- Component code
- Import instructions

tools.name: logo_search
tools.description:
Search and return logos in specified format (JSX, TSX, SVG).
Supports single and multiple logo searches with category filtering.
Can return logos in different themes (light/dark) if available.

When to use this tool:
1. When user types "/logo" command (e.g., "/logo GitHub")
2. When user asks to add a company logo that's not in the local project

Example queries:
- Single company: ["discord"]
- Multiple companies: ["discord", "github", "slack"]
- Specific brand: ["microsoft office"]
- Command style: "/logo GitHub" -> ["github"]
- Request style: "Add Discord logo to the project" -> ["discord"]

- TSX: Returns TypeScript React component
- JSX: Returns JavaScript React component
- SVG: Returns raw SVG markup

- Component name (e.g., DiscordIcon)
- Component code
- Import instructions

tools.name: tools_documentation
tools.description: Get documentation for n8n MCP tools. Call without parameters for quick start guide. Use topic parameter to get documentation for specific tools. Use depth='full' for comprehensive documentation.

topic.description: Tool name (e.g., "search_nodes") or "overview" for general guide. Leave empty for quick reference.

depth.description: Level of detail. "essentials" (default) for quick reference, "full" for comprehensive docs.

tools.name: list_nodes
tools.description: List n8n nodes. Common: list_nodes({limit:200}) for all, list_nodes({category:'trigger'}) for triggers. Package: "n8n-nodes-base" or "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain". Categories: trigger/transform/output/input.

limit.description: Max results (default 50, use 200+ for all)

tools.name: get_node_info
tools.description: Get FULL node schema (100KB+). TIP: Use get_node_essentials first! Returns all properties/operations/credentials. Prefix required: "nodes-base.httpRequest" not "httpRequest".

nodeType.description: Full type: "nodes-base.{name}" or "nodes-langchain.{name}". Examples: nodes-base.httpRequest, nodes-base.webhook, nodes-base.slack

tools.name: search_nodes
tools.description: Search nodes by keywords. Modes: OR (any word), AND (all words), FUZZY (typos OK). Primary nodes ranked first. Examples: "webhook"→Webhook, "http call"→HTTP Request.

query.description: Search terms. Use quotes for exact phrase.

limit.description: Max results (default 20)

tools.name: list_ai_tools
tools.description: List 263 AI-optimized nodes. Note: ANY node can be AI tool! Connect any node to AI Agent's tool port. Community nodes need N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_ALLOW_TOOL_USAGE=true.

tools.name: get_node_documentation
tools.description: Get readable docs with examples/auth/patterns. Better than raw schema! 87% coverage. Format: "nodes-base.slack"

tools.name: get_database_statistics
tools.description: Node stats: 525 total, 263 AI tools, 104 triggers, 87% docs coverage. Verifies MCP working.

tools.name: get_node_essentials
tools.description: Get 10-20 key properties only (<5KB vs 100KB+). USE THIS FIRST! Includes examples. Format: "nodes-base.httpRequest"

tools.name: search_node_properties
tools.description: Find specific properties in a node (auth, headers, body, etc). Returns paths and descriptions.

query.description: Property to find: "auth", "header", "body", "json"

maxResults.description: Max results (default 20)

tools.name: get_node_for_task
tools.description: Get pre-configured node for tasks: post_json_request, receive_webhook, query_database, send_slack_message, etc. Use list_tasks for all.

task.description: Task name. See list_tasks for options.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List task templates by category: HTTP/API, Webhooks, Database, AI, Data Processing, Communication.

tools.name: validate_node_operation
tools.description: Validate node config. Checks required fields, types, operation rules. Returns errors with fixes. Essential for Slack/Sheets/DB nodes.

config.description: Your node configuration. Must include operation fields (resource/operation/action) if the node has multiple operations.

profile.description: Validation profile: minimal (only required fields), runtime (critical errors only), ai-friendly (balanced - default), strict (all checks including best practices)

tools.name: validate_node_minimal
tools.description: Fast check for missing required fields only. No warnings/suggestions. Returns: list of missing fields.

config.description: The node configuration to check

tools.name: get_property_dependencies
tools.description: Shows property dependencies and visibility rules. Example: sendBody=true reveals body fields. Test visibility with optional config.

config.description: Optional partial configuration to check visibility impact

tools.name: get_node_as_tool_info
tools.description: How to use ANY node as AI tool. Shows requirements, use cases, examples. Works for all nodes, not just AI-marked ones.

nodeType.description: Full node type WITH prefix: "nodes-base.slack", "nodes-base.googleSheets", etc.

tools.name: list_node_templates
tools.description: Find templates using specific nodes. 399 community workflows. Use FULL types: "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest".

nodeTypes.description: Array of node types to search for (e.g., ["n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest", "n8n-nodes-base.openAi"])

limit.description: Maximum number of templates to return. Default 10.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Get complete workflow JSON by ID. Ready to import. IDs from list_node_templates or search_templates.

tools.name: search_templates
tools.description: Search templates by name/description keywords. NOT for node types! For nodes use list_node_templates. Example: "chatbot".

query.description: Search query for template names/descriptions. NOT for node types! Examples: "chatbot", "automation", "social media", "webhook". For node-based search use list_node_templates instead.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Default 20.

tools.name: get_templates_for_task

task.description: The type of task to get templates for

tools.name: get_node
tools.description: Get node info with progressive detail levels and multiple modes. Detail: minimal (~200 tokens), standard (~1-2K, default), full (~3-8K). Modes: info (default), docs (markdown documentation), search_properties (find properties), versions/compare/breaking/migrations (version info). Use format='docs' for readable documentation, mode='search_properties' with propertyQuery for finding specific fields.

detail.description: Information detail level. standard=essential properties (recommended), full=everything

mode.description: Operation mode. info=node schema, docs=readable markdown documentation, search_properties=find specific properties, versions/compare/breaking/migrations=version info

toVersion.description: Target version for compare mode (e.g., "2.0"). Defaults to latest if omitted.

propertyQuery.description: For mode=search_properties: search term to find properties (e.g., "auth", "header", "body")

Find organizations that the user has access to in Sentry.

Use this tool when you need to:

- Find an organization's slug to aid other tool requests

tools.name: find_teams
tools.description:
Find teams in an organization in Sentry.

Use this tool when you need to:
- View all teams in a Sentry organization
- Find a team's slug to aid other tool requests

organizationSlug.description: The organization's slug. You can find a existing list of organizations you have access to using the `find_organizations()` tool.

regionUrl.description: The region URL for the organization you're querying, if known. For Sentry's Cloud Service (sentry.io), this is typically the region-specific URL like 'https://us.sentry.io'. For self-hosted Sentry installations, this parameter is usually not needed and should be omitted. You can find the correct regionUrl from the organization details using the `find_organizations()` tool.

regionUrl.description: The region URL for the organization you're querying, if known. For Sentry's Cloud Service (sentry.io), this is typically the region-specific URL like 'https://us.sentry.io'. tools.name: find_releases
tools.description:
Find releases in Sentry.

Use this tool when you need to:
- Find recent releases in a Sentry organization
- Find the most recent version released of a specific project
- Determine when a release was deployed to an environment

<examples>
### Find the most recent releases in the 'my-organization' organization

```
find_releases(organizationSlug='my-organization')
```

### Find releases matching '2ce6a27' in the 'my-organization' organization

```
find_releases(organizationSlug='my-organization', query='2ce6a27')
```
</examples>

<hints>
- If the user passes a parameter in the form of name/otherName, its likely in the format of <organizationSlug>/<projectSlug>.
</hints>

organizationSlug.description: The organization's slug. You can find a existing list of organizations you have access to using the `find_organizations()` tool.

regionUrl.description: The region URL for the organization you're querying, if known. For Sentry's Cloud Service (sentry.io), this is typically the region-specific URL like 'https://us.sentry.io'. For self-hosted Sentry installations, this parameter is usually not needed and should be omitted. You can find the correct regionUrl from the organization details using the `find_organizations()` tool.

projectSlug.description: The project's slug. This will default to all projects you have access to. It is encouraged to specify this when possible.

query.description: Search for versions which contain the provided string.

tools.name: get_issue_details
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific Sentry issue by ID.

🔍 USE THIS TOOL WHEN USERS:
- Provide a specific issue ID (e.g., 'CLOUDFLARE-MCP-41', 'PROJECT-123')
- Ask to 'explain [ISSUE-ID]', 'tell me about [ISSUE-ID]'
- Want details/stacktrace/analysis for a known issue
- Provide a Sentry issue URL

❌ DO NOT USE for:
- General searching or listing issues (use search_issues)
- Root cause analysis (use analyze_issue_with_seer)

TRIGGER PATTERNS:
- 'Explain ISSUE-123' → use get_issue_details
- 'Tell me about PROJECT-456' → use get_issue_details
- 'What happened in [issue URL]' → use get_issue_details

<examples>
### Explain specific issue
```
get_issue_details(organizationSlug='my-organization', issueId='CLOUDFLARE-MCP-41')
```

### Get details for event ID
```
get_issue_details(organizationSlug='my-organization', eventId='c49541c747cb4d8aa3efb70ca5aba243')
```
</examples>

<hints>
- If the user provides the `issueUrl`, you can ignore the other parameters.
- If the user provides `issueId` or `eventId` (only one is needed), `organizationSlug` is required.
</hints>

organizationSlug.description: The organization's slug. You can find a existing list of organizations you have access to using the `find_organizations()` tool.

regionUrl.description: The region URL for the organization you're querying, if known. For Sentry's Cloud Service (sentry.io), this is typically the region-specific URL like 'https://us.sentry.io'. For self-hosted Sentry installations, this parameter is usually not needed and should be omitted. You can find the correct regionUrl from the organization details using the `find_organizations()` tool.

issueUrl.description: The URL of the issue. e.g. https://my-organization.sentry.io/issues/PROJECT-1Z43

tools.name: get_trace_details
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific Sentry trace by ID.

🔍 USE THIS TOOL WHEN USERS:
- Provide a specific trace ID (e.g., 'a4d1aae7216b47ff8117cf4e09ce9d0a')
- Ask to 'show me trace [TRACE-ID]', 'explain trace [TRACE-ID]'
- Want high-level overview and link to view trace details in Sentry
- Need trace statistics and span breakdown

❌ DO NOT USE for:
- General searching for traces (use search_events with trace queries)
- Individual span details (this shows trace overview)

TRIGGER PATTERNS:
- 'Show me trace abc123' → use get_trace_details
- 'Explain trace a4d1aae7216b47ff8117cf4e09ce9d0a' → use get_trace_details
- 'What is trace [trace-id]' → use get_trace_details

<examples>
### Get trace overview
```
get_trace_details(organizationSlug='my-organization', traceId='a4d1aae7216b47ff8117cf4e09ce9d0a')
```
</examples>

<hints>
- Trace IDs are 32-character hexadecimal strings
</hints>

organizationSlug.description: The organization's slug. You can find a existing list of organizations you have access to using the `find_organizations()` tool.

regionUrl.description: The region URL for the organization you're querying, if known. For Sentry's Cloud Service (sentry.io), this is typically the region-specific URL like 'https://us.sentry.io'. For self-hosted Sentry installations, this parameter is usually not needed and should be omitted. You can find the correct regionUrl from the organization details using the `find_organizations()` tool.

tools.name: get_event_attachment
tools.description:
Download attachments from a Sentry event.

Use this tool when you need to:
- Download files attached to a specific event
- Access screenshots, log files, or other attachments uploaded with an error report
- Retrieve attachment metadata and download URLs

<examples>
### Download a specific attachment by ID

```
get_event_attachment(organizationSlug='my-organization', projectSlug='my-project', eventId='c49541c747cb4d8aa3efb70ca5aba243', attachmentId='12345')

Analyze CPU profiling data to identify performance bottlenecks and detect regressions.

USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
- User asks why a specific endpoint/transaction is slow
- User wants to understand where CPU time is spent
- User asks about performance bottlenecks
- User wants to compare performance between time periods
- User shares a Sentry profile URL

RETURNS:
- Hot paths (call stacks consuming the most CPU time)
- Performance percentiles (p75, p95, p99) for each function
- User code vs library code breakdown
- Actionable recommendations for optimization
- Regression analysis when comparing periods

get_profile(
  organizationSlug='my-org',
  transactionName='/api/users',
  projectSlugOrId='backend'
)
```

### Compare performance between periods
```
get_profile(
  organizationSlug='my-org',
  transactionName='/api/users',
  projectSlugOrId='backend',
  statsPeriod='7d',
  compareAgainstPeriod='14d'
)
```
</examples>

Update a Sentry issue's status or assignment.

Use this to resolve, reopen, assign, or ignore an issue.

<examples>

<hints>

- At least one of `status` or `assignedTo` is required.
- `assignedTo` format: `user:ID` or `team:ID_OR_SLUG`.
- Use `whoami` to find your user ID for self-assignment.
- Status values: `resolved`, `resolvedInNextRelease`, `unresolved`, `ignored`.
- `status='ignored'` defaults to `ignoreMode='untilEscalating'`.
- Ignore modes: `untilEscalating`, `forever`, `forDuration`, `untilOccurrenceCount`, `untilUserCount`.
- Matching ignore inputs are `ignoreDurationMinutes`, `ignoreCount` + optional `ignoreWindowMinutes`, or `ignoreUserCount` + optional `ignoreUserWindowMinutes`.
- To switch an already ignored issue between `untilEscalating`, `forever`, and condition-based ignore modes, first set `status='unresolved'`, then ignore it again with the new rule.
- `reason` is optional. When provided, it will be posted as a comment on the issue's activity feed explaining why the action was taken.
</hints>

tools.name: search_events
tools.description:
Search Sentry events and replays. Use for event counts/statistics.

`query` can be natural language or Sentry search syntax. With an agent configured, it fixes dataset, query, fields, and sort before running.

Supports TWO query types:
1. AGGREGATIONS (counts, sums, averages): 'how many errors', 'total tokens'
2. Individual events with timestamps: 'error logs from last hour'

Datasets:
- errors: Exception/crash events with stack traces, usually grouped into issues
- logs: Application log entries, including error-severity log messages
- spans: Raw trace/span events for performance, AI/LLM calls, requests, and operations
- metrics: Metric rows and aggregates: counters, gauges, distributions, values
- profiles: Transaction/continuous profile results, profile IDs, profiled transactions
- replays: Session replay results: rage clicks, dead clicks, visited pages, replay users
If the user says logs, log messages, error logs, or warning logs, choose logs instead of errors.

Replay searches return replay lists only; replay count()/avg()/sum() are not supported.

NOT for grouped issue lists (use search_issues) or app screenshots/images (use get_latest_base_snapshot).

<examples>
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', query='how many errors today')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='errors', query='level:error')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='errors', fields=['issue', 'count()'], sort='-count()')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='spans', query='span.op:db', sort='-span.duration')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='replays', query='count_errors:>0', sort='-count_errors')
</examples>

<hints>
- If the user passes a parameter in the form of name/otherName, it's likely in the format of <organizationSlug>/<projectSlug>.
- Parse org/project notation directly without calling find_organizations or find_projects.
- Use fields with aggregate functions like count(), avg(), sum() for statistics
- Sort by -count() for most common, -timestamp for newest
</hints>

tools.name: get_sentry_resource
tools.description:
Fetch a Sentry resource by URL or by type and ID. Pass a Sentry URL directly and the resource type is auto-detected.

Supports issues, events, traces, spans, AI conversations, replays, breadcrumbs, and preprod snapshots.
Sentry URLs require authentication that this tool handles.

get_sentry_resource(url='https://sentry.io/issues/PROJECT-123/')

get_sentry_resource(url='https://sentry.io/issues/PROJECT-123/', resourceType='breadcrumbs')

### By type and ID
get_sentry_resource(resourceType='issue', organizationSlug='my-org', resourceId='PROJECT-123')

### Span by trace and span ID
get_sentry_resource(resourceType='span', organizationSlug='my-org', resourceId='a4d1aae7216b47ff8117cf4e09ce9d0a:aa8e7f3384ef4ff5')

get_sentry_resource(resourceType='replay', organizationSlug='my-org', resourceId='7e07485f-12f9-416b-8b14-26260799b51f')

get_sentry_resource(resourceType='ai_conversation', organizationSlug='my-org', resourceId='conversation-123')

get_sentry_resource(url='https://sentry.sentry.io/preprod/snapshots/241539/')

### View a specific changed snapshot image
get_sentry_resource(url='https://sentry.sentry.io/preprod/snapshots/241539/?selectedSnapshot=login_screen.png')
</examples>

tools.name: search_events
tools.description:
Search Sentry events and replays. Use for event counts/statistics.

`query` can be natural language or Sentry search syntax. With an agent configured, it fixes dataset, query, fields, and sort before running.

Supports TWO query types:
1. AGGREGATIONS (counts, sums, averages): 'how many errors', 'total tokens'
2. Individual events with timestamps: 'error logs from last hour'

Datasets:
- errors: Exception/crash events with stack traces, usually grouped into issues
- logs: Application log entries, including error-severity log messages
- spans: Raw trace/span events for performance, AI/LLM calls, requests, and operations
- metrics: Metric rows and aggregates: counters, gauges, distributions, values
- profiles: Transaction/continuous profile results, profile IDs, profiled transactions
- replays: Session replay results: rage clicks, dead clicks, visited pages, replay users
If the user says logs, log messages, error logs, or warning logs, choose logs instead of errors.

Replay searches return replay lists only; replay count()/avg()/sum() are not supported.

NOT for grouped issue lists (use search_issues) or app screenshots/images (use get_latest_base_snapshot).

<examples>
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', query='how many errors today')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='errors', query='level:error')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='errors', fields=['issue', 'count()'], sort='-count()')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='spans', query='span.op:db', sort='-span.duration')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='replays', query='count_errors:>0', sort='-count_errors')

tools.name: search_events
tools.description:
Search Sentry events and replays. Use for event counts/statistics.

`query` can be natural language or Sentry search syntax. With an agent configured, it fixes dataset, query, fields, and sort before running.

Supports TWO query types:
1. AGGREGATIONS (counts, sums, averages): 'how many errors', 'total tokens'
2. Individual events with timestamps: 'error logs from last hour'

Datasets:
- errors: Exception/crash events with stack traces, usually grouped into issues
- logs: Application log entries, including error-severity log messages
- spans: Raw trace/span events for performance, AI/LLM calls, requests, and operations
- metrics: Metric rows and aggregates: counters, gauges, distributions, values
- profiles: Transaction/continuous profile results, profile IDs, profiled transactions
- replays: Session replay results: rage clicks, dead clicks, visited pages, replay users
If the user says logs, log messages, error logs, or warning logs, choose logs instead of errors.

Replay searches return replay lists only; replay count()/avg()/sum() are not supported.

NOT for grouped issue lists (use search_issues) or app screenshots/images (use get_latest_base_snapshot).

<examples>
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', query='how many errors today')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='errors', query='level:error')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='errors', fields=['issue', 'count()'], sort='-count()')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='spans', query='span.op:db', sort='-span.duration')
search_events(organizationSlug='my-org', dataset='replays', query='count_errors:>0', sort='-count_errors')
</examples>

<hints>

- Parse org/project notation directly without calling find_organizations or find_projects.
- Use fields with aggregate functions like count(), avg(), sum() for statistics
- Sort by -count() for most common, -timestamp for newest
</hints>

- With ?selectedSnapshot=<image_file_name>: returns the image preview and metadata. Use the Sentry tool `get_snapshot_image` for full-resolution image bytes.

Resource IDs:
- monitor: <monitorSlug>
- snapshot: <snapshotId>

<examples>
get_sentry_resource(url='https://sentry.io/issues/PROJECT-123/')
get_sentry_resource(resourceType='issue', organizationSlug='my-org', resourceId='PROJECT-123')
get_sentry_resource(resourceType='ai_conversation', organizationSlug='my-org', resourceId='conversation-123')
get_sentry_resource(url='https://sentry.sentry.io/preprod/snapshots/123/')
get_sentry_resource(url='https://sentry.sentry.io/preprod/snapshots/123/?selectedSnapshot=login_screen.png')
</examples>

url.description: Sentry URL. The resource type is auto-detected from the URL pattern.

resourceType.description: Resource type. With a URL, can override a span-focused trace URL with `trace`. Use `monitor` with a monitor slug only when inspect monitor tools are available or `snapshot` with a snapshot artifact ID.

resourceId.description: Resource identifier: issue shortId (e.g., 'PROJECT-123'), event ID, trace ID, agent conversation ID, replay ID, monitor slug when inspect monitor tools are available, or snapshot artifact ID. Required when not using a URL.

organizationSlug.description: The organization's slug. You can find a existing list of organizations you have access to using the `find_organizations()` tool.

tools.name: search_sentry_tools
tools.description:
Search the available Sentry MCP tool catalog by name and description.

Many Sentry operations are intentionally not exposed as top-level tools. Use this for any Sentry-related task when you do not see an obvious direct tool, including long-tail inspection, project management, documentation lookup, preprod snapshots, attachments, DSNs, releases, teams, and issue-specific pivots.

Use this tool when you need to:
- Find the right Sentry operation for a task
- Discover catalog tools and their schemas for a task
- Inspect the executable JSON input schema for an available tool

<examples>
search_sentry_tools(query='list projects')
search_sentry_tools(query='issue details')
search_sentry_tools(query='find dsn', limit=5)
search_sentry_tools(query='snapshot image')
</examples>

<hints>
- Results only include tools available in the current session.
- If a Sentry operation is not listed as a direct tool, search here before deciding it is unavailable.
- Returned schemas already account for active organization, project, and region constraints.
- Use the returned name and schema when executing a catalog result.
- This tool returns structured JSON. Do not parse markdown from its text content.
</hints>

query.description: Natural language keywords describing the Sentry operation, resource, or workflow to find.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching tools to return, up to 20.

tools.name: execute_sentry_tool
tools.description:
Execute an available Sentry MCP tool discovered through search_sentry_tools.

Use this tool when you need to:
- Call a Sentry operation returned by search_sentry_tools
- Execute a tool by name using arguments that match its returned schema

<examples>
execute_sentry_tool(name='find_projects', arguments={ organizationSlug: 'my-org' })
execute_sentry_tool(name='whoami', arguments={})
</examples>

<hints>
- Use search_sentry_tools first if you are not sure which name or arguments to pass.
- Arguments are validated against the target tool's schema before execution.
- Active organization, project, and region constraints are injected automatically.
</hints>

name.description: The name of the available tool to execute.

arguments.description: Arguments for the target tool, matching the schema returned by search_sentry_tools.
